name: phantom-plugins
description: Plugins for Phantom, installed on demand instead of bundled

plugins.name: Phantom Database Console
plugins.description: Connect to MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, H2, AWS JDBC Wrapper, Redshift, Athena, Oracle, SQL Server, SQLite, ClickHouse, Snowflake or any JDBC driver you add, and run SQL from the editor: highlighting for .sql files, Ctrl+Enter to run the statement at the caret, results in a sortable grid, and a lazily loaded schema tree. Drivers are data you can edit: each is found in the project's own dependencies, the local Gradle/Maven cache or jars you choose, and is downloaded from Maven only when you ask (Download, Test Connection). Nothing runs at startup. A data source in manual-commit mode keeps changes in an open transaction: review them in the Database Changes tool window and commit or roll them back; closing the project asks first. A result from one table with its primary key can be edited in the grid, and Compare With on a schema diffs two schemas and writes the SQL to make them match. SQL in Spring Data `@Query(nativeQuery = true)`, `@NativeQuery` and JdbcTemplate / JdbcClient strings is highlighted and completed like a console. JPA entities are checked against the data source's schema (tables and columns that do not exist, nullable columns mapped to non-null attributes), and @Table / @Column names complete from it. A data source can have a color (as in DataGrip): its consoles and .sql files get it as editor background and tab color, its tree rows and result tabs too. A console or .sql file can run in a chosen schema (catalog in MySQL), which unqualified table names in completion and checks also resolve against. The Database tree groups each schema's tables, views, routines, triggers and sequences in folders, can be filtered by name, and Navigate → Database Object (a Database tab in Search Everywhere) finds loaded tables, views, routines and columns without connecting. A data source can have several consoles (New Console), kept in Scratches and Consoles. In the editor: after JOIN, completion offers the tables a foreign key links to the ones in FROM with their ON clause, and after ON whole join conditions from foreign keys (then by column name); SQL (Phantom) live templates sel, selc, selw, ins, upd, del, crt; Find Usages and Rename of tables, views and columns across .sql files, consoles and SQL strings (and JPA mappings), changing SQL text only, never the database; unknown tables and columns are reported with quick fixes. Connections can go through an SSH tunnel (password, key file or OpenSSH agent; unknown host keys confirmed and added to ~/.ssh/known_hosts) and use SSL (mode, CA, client certificate and key mapped to each driver's properties), set in the SSH/SSL tab. Diagram on a schema or selected tables draws them with their foreign keys (pan, zoom, drag, PNG export); Import Data from CSV on a table maps columns by header and inserts in batches in one transaction; Explain Plan shows the plan as a tree with cost, rows and time and the costliest step highlighted. Results grid: WHERE / ORDER BY fields with column completion and history, header clicks sorting a table on the server, a Value Viewer (JSON, XML, hex, images), Transpose, selection sum/avg/min/max, pinned result tabs, and Copy/Export as TSV, CSV, JSON, SQL INSERT, Markdown or HTML (a whole table streamed to a file). 0.17.0: unreachable routine code, cursor state, routine side effects vs. NO SQL/READS SQL DATA, invalid date/time literals, LOAD DATA paths, too many joins, SQL files without a data source; CREATE TABLE to entity marker. 0.17.1: a data source entry the IDE cannot read is skipped instead of breaking the Database Changes tool window and the JPA schema checks. 0.17.2: no completion right after a number (Enter no longer turns `id = 2` into `id = 2EMAIL`); opening a table no longer logs a read-access error. 0.18.0: as in DataGrip: Make Global keeps a data source (with its passwords) in the IDE for every project; passwords saved Forever, Until restart or Never, read once per IDE run, and asked again when the database refuses them; DataGrip's shortcuts in the tree, editor and grid; grid edits wait as changes until Submit (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) or Submit and Commit, with Revert Selected and Submit Changes Immediately; Set NULL / Set DEFAULT, Select Row / Column, Edit Filter Criteria; SQL Generator and Copy DDL; data source groups, copy, paste and duplicate; single session mode or a session per console with a session switcher, Sessions and the Services tool window; schema scope and introspection levels. 0.18.1: Add Row and Clone Row in the grid, inserted on Submit; Preview Pending Changes. 0.18.2: dates and times in the grid show as stored and save as typed (east of UTC a TIMESTAMP or TIME showed hours early and a DATE the day before); changed, new and deleted cells are colored until Submit; a row inserted on Submit shows its generated key and defaults, so it can be edited again. 0.19.0: grid changes not yet submitted are asked about (Submit, Discard, Cancel) before the result is replaced or its tab closed; Add Row starts editing the new row and shows unfilled cells as <default>; Run 'file.sql' from the project view and editor tab; Dump to File and Restore from File with mysqldump / mysql and pg_dump / psql (not over SSH); TIMESTAMP fractional seconds show in the grid. 0.19.1: MySQL's DATETIME and TIMESTAMP(n) show their fraction and open the calendar on their value; dump and restore reach localhost over TCP; all data source passwords are kept in one keychain entry, so macOS asks once, not once per data source. 0.20.0: Copy As and the grid's Data Extractor list (used by Copy, Cmd/Ctrl+C) add SQL INSERT Multirow, SQL UPDATE, One-Row, XML and Pretty; Paste of copied rows into the grid fills the cells and adds rows. 0.21.0: Filter by on a cell (=, <>, LIKE, IS NULL, IN) adds to WHERE and runs; Column Statistics; pasted text takes the column's type; Copy Table To copies a table's rows into another schema or data source, creating the table when it is missing. 0.22.0: Full-text Search on a data source or schema finds a text (or number) in every table and opens the matching rows; Export saves Excel (.xlsx) workbooks, a whole table page by page too. 0.23.0: Quick Documentation on tables and columns in SQL; Structure view of SQL files; Run Again and Auto Refresh for query results; Compare Content of two tables, with the SQL that makes one match the other. 0.24.0: a join's result is editable: each cell updates its own table by that table's primary key. 0.24.1: the format picked in the result toolbar's Copy As stays what Copy (Cmd/Ctrl+C) uses, in new results too, and is checked in the list. 0.24.2: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter runs the statement in a console or .sql file again instead of splitting the line, and the Database tree's toolbar and commands no longer hold up the IDE by reading the clipboard. 0.25.0: ERD Design (.erd files kept in git): draw tables and relations, load a schema from a data source, and get CREATE or ALTER SQL against it; the SQL editor underlines misspelled keywords, missing commas, tables and conditions, clauses out of order and unclosed parentheses and quotes as you type, with quick fixes, and marks where a failed statement went wrong; completion by clause (keywords, functions, types, subquery and CTE columns) that opens after a dot and after FROM or JOIN; colors by what a name is (Color Scheme → SQL (Phantom)); parameter info for built-in functions, column names before INSERT values, Expand * to columns, folding, paired quotes, Extend Selection by clause and parentheses, Surround With, Complete Current Statement, and a Code Style page (indent, keyword case); the Database tree's toolbar keeps Add, Refresh, New Console and Data, the rest under More. 0.25.1: Diagram and ERD Design draw tables as cards (header band, key and link icons, types aligned right) on a dotted grid, with relations between the columns they join and a crow's foot on the many side. 0.25.2: SQL that MyBatis Support injects as a whole statement shows syntax errors. 0.25.3: the syntax check is open to MyBatis Support for statements with <choose> and ${}. 0.25.4: Run and Explain take only the statement at the caret when the one above has no ; and consoles open without the Non-Project Files Protection prompt. 0.25.5: the Java and Kotlin part (SQL in strings, JPA entities against the schema) loads in Phantom again. 0.25.6: Cmd/Ctrl+click on a table or column name in SQL selects it in the Database tree also when the tool window was not open yet, and says so when the tree does not show it. 0.25.7: Copy on a Database tree node puts its name on the clipboard, not the node object. 0.25.8: Modify Table shows and edits column comments and has room for long column and index names; changing a MySQL column keeps its comment and AUTO_INCREMENT (MODIFY COLUMN restated the column without them).

plugins.name: Spring Support
plugins.description: Spring support for Java and Kotlin: bean injection navigation in both directions, an autowiring inspection, correct unused analysis for Spring-managed code, Spring MVC handlers for the Endpoints tool window, Spring Security path and expression support, and Kafka/RabbitMQ/JMS sender-receiver navigation. 0.4.0: proxy pitfalls (self-invocation of @Transactional/@Cacheable/@Async, private/final/static proxied methods, Kotlin classes not opened by kotlin-spring), @Scheduled/@Async/@EventListener contracts, field and static injection, duplicate bean names, @Scope values, @Sql paths, @DirtiesContext, publishEvent ↔ listener gutters, @Qualifier/@DependsOn bean name completion and Ctrl+B. Wave 6: @Value placeholders (follows spring.config.import), SpEL syntax, cache names, caching on interfaces, @Qualifier/@DependsOn near-miss names, MVC path variables, endpoint and AOP advice gutters, method security not enabled, pointcut syntax. Wave 7: @Cacheable+@CachePut, abstract beans, @Value literal types, @Bean method shape, scan packages, AspectJ autoproxy, @Autowired outside beans, resource locations, @TestBean factories, @Around/pointcut/argNames/@DeclareParents, Security debug/self-invocation/bean refs. Wave 8: @Bean init/destroy methods, @Lookup, Resource @Value, @Profile expressions and unknown profiles, bean name convention, argNames bindings; cache, @Scheduled and @Import gutters. Waves 9-10: @Transactional/@Async, component scan and advised-method gutters; Spring 7 API versioning checks; HTTP header and media type typos; broken @Value placeholders; JDK proxy injection. Wave 11: test transaction pitfalls, @Value with @Qualifier/@Resource, removed @Required, @Qualifier bean type, ROLE_ prefix misuse.

plugins.name: Spring Boot Support
plugins.description: Spring Boot support: File → New → Project → Spring Boot generates projects with Spring Initializr, and application*.yml / application*.properties get completion and quick documentation for keys and values, from library metadata and the project's own @ConfigurationProperties, in Java and Kotlin. An Actuator tab beside the console of a running app (health, beans, mappings, environment, polled only while shown; only for modules with spring-boot-starter-actuator), and completion and Ctrl+B for ${...} placeholders in @Value from the project's application.yml/properties and Spring Boot metadata. Wave 7: datasource driver missing, config key <-> @Value/@ConfigurationProperties gutters, spring.config.import files count as config. Wave 8: profile override gutters between application-<profile> and base config, @SpringBootApplication -> config files. Wave 9: @ConditionalOnProperty, @EnableConfigurationProperties, test property, @ConfigurationProperties field and profile value gutters. Wave 11: unread bootstrap.yml, Spring Cloud Stream bindings without a function bean.

plugins.name: JPA Support
plugins.description: JPA, Hibernate and Spring Data JPA for Java and Kotlin: JPQL in @Query with completion and errors, derived query method checks, a @Modifying check, entity mapping checks, and repository/entity gutter navigation. An Entity Diagram tool window: entities, columns and relations drawn from the code, copyable as a Mermaid erDiagram. 0.3.0: entity checks (several @Id, no-arg constructor, mappedBy, raw collections, converters), attribute checks (@Column on associations, LAZY on the inverse @OneToOne, @ManyToMany cascade REMOVE, unmapped entity fields, @Enumerated), Kotlin entity checks (kotlin-jpa/all-open, data class, val attributes, read-only collections), Lombok on entities, repository return and parameter types and Pageable. Wave 6: JPQL undeclared aliases and function arity, entity graph attributes, entity listener callback signatures. Wave 7: entity listener usage, named queries, JPQL in createQuery, Kotlin non-null vs nullable columns, Lombok @AllArgsConstructor without no-arg. Wave 9: derived query JPQL gutter, attribute <-> repository methods, @EntityGraph navigation. Wave 11: SQL injection through string-built JDBC/JPA queries, Criteria attribute names (check, completion, Ctrl+B), Jakarta Data repositories, Hibernate @Find, Spring Data JDBC aggregates and mappings.

plugins.name: MyBatis Support
plugins.description: MyBatis mapper support (what MyBatisX does): interface ↔ XML statement gutters, statement id / resultMap / refid / resultType / property references with completion, rename and errors, mapper methods without a statement with a quick fix that writes it, #{...} parameter completion, and SQL highlighting and completion in mapper XML and @Select/@Insert/@Update/@Delete with Phantom Database Console. 0.1.1: Go to Implementation from mapper method calls opens the XML statement; Cmd+click on #{a.b}, <if test>, <foreach collection> and @Select placeholders goes to the parameter, property or foreach item. 0.2.0 (with Phantom Database Console 0.25.2): dynamic tags read as MyBatis builds them (<where> AND/OR, <set> commas, <trim>, <include>), syntax errors in whole statements, a run icon on each statement that runs it in the console asking for #{} values, and Reformat Code formats the SQL of plain statements. 0.3.0 (with Phantom Database Console 0.25.3): syntax errors in each <choose> branch and with ${}, Run asks which <if> parts and <choose> branches to take and builds <where>/<set>/<trim> by MyBatis rules, and Reformat Code formats statements with dynamic tags. 0.3.1: loads in Phantom again (Java classes come from the Java plugin modules), so mapper SQL highlights and the inspections run.

plugins.name: Reactive Streams Support
plugins.description: Reactor and RxJava checks for Java and Kotlin: a Mono, Flux or RxJava source created and dropped without being subscribed, and blocking calls inside reactive operators.

plugins.name: Ktor Support
plugins.description: Ktor server routes from the routing DSL, including routes in Route extension functions with the prefixes of their callers, in the Endpoints tool window.

plugins.name: Kubernetes Support
plugins.description: Helm chart templates: .Values completion and navigation from values.yaml, .Release/.Chart fields, include/define navigation, and a warning for values that values.yaml does not define. 0.2.0: manifest checks for built-in kinds (removed API versions, unknown and missing keys with key completion, duplicate env vars, selector/template label mismatch); YAML in Markdown fences is skipped. Wave 7: unknown kinds, enum values, deprecated keys/resources, server-set fields, Chart.yaml. Wave 8: gutters Service <-> workloads, ConfigMap/Secret/ServiceAccount references, Ingress backends. Wave 10: kinds that are not stored (reviews, Binding, Eviction). Wave 11: deprecated labels/annotations, required list-item keys, unknown Helm templates, risky whitespace trimming, define to include markers.

plugins.name: Phantom Profiler
plugins.description: CPU and allocation profiling for Java and Kotlin with Java Flight Recorder: a Profile action next to Run and Debug, a Profiler tool window that records any running JVM, and a .jfr viewer with flame graph, call tree, hot methods, allocations and GC summary. Profile also works on Gradle run configurations: tests run by Gradle and applications delegated to Gradle, one recording per forked JVM.

plugins.name: Docker Support
plugins.description: Docker Compose through the docker CLI: run icons on compose services, a Docker Compose run configuration shown in Services, and a Docker tool window listing containers by compose project with start, stop, restart, remove, logs and compose down. Polls only while open. 0.2.0: Compose checks (unknown keys and values, undefined services/networks/volumes with Ctrl+B and completion, missing image, unquoted base-60 ports, duplicate container names) and Dockerfile checks (continuations, argument counts, exec form, heredocs, stages, COPY/ADD paths). Wave 7: Compose pull_policy and network_mode values. Wave 8: Compose build -> Dockerfile and depends_on gutters, Dockerfile stage Ctrl+B. Wave 10: COPY/ADD here-documents BuildKit rejects. Wave 11: FROM ... AS stage to its usages marker.

plugins.name: Phantom Key-Value Console
plugins.description: A key browser and console for Redis-compatible servers (Redis, Valkey, KeyDB…): keys by SCAN pattern, values of every type with JSON indented, delete, and a redis-cli style command line with history. Password, ACL user, database and TLS. Connects only while the Redis tool window is shown.

plugins.name: Kafka Support
plugins.description: An Apache Kafka browser: topics with partitions and offsets, latest/earliest/since-time messages read without joining a group, sending with key, headers and partition, consumer group lag, create and delete topics. SASL/SSL via client properties in the password safe.

plugins.name: Bean Validation Support
plugins.description: Bean Validation checks for Java and Kotlin: contradictory bounds (@Min above @Max, @Size min above max), constraints on types they cannot validate, Kotlin constructor properties whose constraint lands on the parameter (quick fix: @field:), nested objects with constraints but no @Valid, and Spring beans with method constraints but no @Validated. Wave 7: custom @Constraint definitions.

plugins.name: Phantom Migrations
plugins.description: Flyway and Liquibase checks: migration names Flyway skips (single underscore, lower-case prefix, no description) and duplicate versions in db/migration and spring.flyway.locations; duplicate changeset id and author and missing include/includeAll paths in XML, YAML and formatted SQL changelogs. Wave 8: Flyway previous/next migration gutters, Liquibase include navigation. 0.3.0: unresolved Liquibase changelog properties.

plugins.name: OpenAPI Support
plugins.description: OpenAPI and Swagger specs in YAML and JSON: $ref navigation to local pointers and other files, #/components/... completion, unresolved $ref errors, and gutter links between a spec operation and its handler (Spring MVC and any framework in the Endpoints view). Wave 10: specs not recognized because of a misspelled version key, unsupported versions, unknown top-level keys.

plugins.name: Phantom HTTP Client
plugins.description: HTTP requests in .http / .rest files, run from the editor: file and http-client.env.json environment variables, import and run lines to reuse requests from other files, a run gutter per request plus Run All, checks for common mistakes (broken JSON bodies, headers the client can't send, unknown methods, missing ###, broken {{}}, plain http to remote hosts), and a response view with status, headers and a formatted body. Moved out of the Phantom core so it updates like any other plugin. 0.2.0: auth ids from Security.Auths (resolution, completion, Ctrl+B, unknown id and configuration checks), URL scheme and encoding checks.

plugins.name: Phantom Icon Pack
plugins.description: Colored file and folder icons by name and extension from the Material Icon Theme (Philipp Kief, MIT). Java files show the Java cup and Kotlin files the Kotlin logo, also where a file shows as its class (Project view, navigation bar, editor tabs); Java classes show Material icons by kind. Source, test and resource roots get their own folder colors. Moved out of the Phantom bundle (Phantom File Icons, dev.phantom.icons): turn that one off if your Phantom still bundles it.

plugins.name: Phantom AI Integration
plugins.description: Claude Code and Codex next to your projects (0.3.16): a tree of the current project's worktrees and agent sessions beside the agent terminals in one tool window, a board editor tab, an agent dashboard, usage in the status bar and opt-in remote control from another device's browser. Select code in the editor and type an AI command to leave an AI memo (kept in memory only, following its code as lines move), then send the checked memos to a session as one prompt, queued while that session is busy. Agents open files at a line in the editor and read what you are looking at through Phantom's own MCP server, with no setup. A small public API, dev.phantom.ai.api, lets other plugins read sessions (with the subagents each started, since 0.3.1, and what each is doing right now, since 0.3.8) and worktrees and focus or start a session. Agents keep running in tmux when their project window closes and reattach when it reopens. Needs Phantom Workspaces. 0.3.22: agents read one declaration (read_symbol), replace one or insert next to it (replace_symbol, insert_code) as undoable IDE edits, and read the end of a Run console filtered by a pattern (get_run_output). 0.3.23: with Phantom Database Console, agents list its data sources, tables and columns and run read-only queries (list_databases, list_tables, describe_table, query_database); passwords stay in Phantom. 0.3.24: agent teams, detached-session reattach, the hook server and Remote Control wait until they are needed. 0.3.25: agents draft changes with draft_sql, which writes the SQL into the data source's console in the editor and never runs it; reads stay read-only and rolled back.

plugins.name: Phantom AI Visualization
plugins.description: The agent sessions of Phantom AI Integration as an isometric pixel-art place (0.6.2): each worktree is a floor and an office: the first session opened in it is the CEO in an office of its own, a session leading subagents gets a team area with its subordinates seated by role, the rest share the open desks, and a session waiting for an answer lines up before the CEO for sign-off (결재); each live session is a cute big-eyed person drawn at twice the scene's pixel density: typing, waiting with a raised hand, holding a coffee or asleep. A label over every head says what the agent is doing right now (Edit Foo.kt, Bash: ./gradlew test, 권한 요청) and running subagents sit beside their lead as full-size subordinates, each with its own label. Click a person to focus its terminal, an empty desk to start Claude or Codex. Opens from its AI Visualization tool window icon or Tools | Open AI Visualization; six themes in Settings | Tools | Phantom AI Visualization: Warm Wood (A), Modern Bright (B), Night Shift (C), Restroom Cleaning (D, with a cat and a corgi), Kitchen (E) and Construction Site (F). Needs Phantom AI Integration 0.3.8.

plugins.name: Phantom Tab Groups
plugins.description: Editor tab groups, as in a web browser: from a tab's context menu put tabs into a named, colored group, collapse the group to its first tab (showing the group's name and size) and expand it again, rename, recolor, ungroup or close the group; drag tabs in and out. A group reads as one piece: a line in the group's color runs under all its tabs, they get a faint background in that color, and the group's name is a chip in that color on its first tab; a click on the chip collapses or opens the group and dragging it moves the whole group, as in Chrome. Groups belong to each editor split and are kept with the project; collapsing only hides tabs, files stay open and are never closed by the tab limit. Moved out of the Phantom bundle; uses only the public platform API. 0.2.8: the tab group code loads only once a project has tab groups.

plugins.name: Phantom Workspaces
plugins.description: All open projects as tabs of one window (0.6.1): a tab strip above the editor lists every open project (click to switch, middle-click or the close button to close, drag to reorder), and only the project in front has a window on screen, the others hidden behind it, so there is one window and a project you open comes in as a new tab. Project windows share one size, position and maximized state; a project switched to also takes full screen. Every project tab takes the tool window layout of the one in front (stripe sides and order, open tool windows, sizes). A tab can be detached into a window of its own (context menu or drag it out of the strip) and attached back from the Window menu, and two can be shown side by side (Open Side by Side), resizing together. Next/previous project: Window | Next Project Window. Works on every OS, no native window tabs; off in Settings | Advanced Settings | Phantom Workspaces. Moved out of the Phantom bundle so it updates like any other plugin. 0.6.2: with one project open, the hidden tab strip builds nothing at startup.

plugins.name: Phantom Strings
plugins.description: Text conversions on each selection, or on the identifier at the caret: switch case (camelCase, snake_case, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, kebab-case, PascalCase in turn) or convert to one of them, dot.case, words, upper and lower case; escape and unescape Java/Kotlin strings and HTML/XML, URL and Base64 encode and decode; sort, reverse, shuffle, deduplicate and trim lines, remove blank ones. Alt+M opens them in a popup with speed search; also under Edit and the editor's context menu. Works with several carets. Replaces the StringManipulation plugin: turn that one off.

plugins.name: Phantom Rainbow
plugins.description: Brackets colored by nesting depth, (), [] and {} each counted on their own, in every language whose brackets the IDE matches; each line's indentation colored by level, as wide as the file's indent size. Either can be turned off under Settings | Editor | Rainbow; the colors are under Editor | Color Scheme | Rainbow. Replaces Rainbow Brackets and Indent Rainbow: turn those off.

plugins.name: Phantom Ignore Files
plugins.description: .dockerignore, .npmignore, .helmignore, .prettierignore, .eslintignore, .stylelintignore, .gcloudignore and .vscodeignore edited like .gitignore: highlighting, path completion and navigation, comments, duplicate entry checks. New | Ignore File from Template adds templates (Java, Kotlin, Gradle, Maven, IntelliJ, VS Code, macOS, Windows, Linux, Node, Python, Go, Rust, Docker) to any of these files or .gitignore, skipping lines the file already has. Replaces the .ignore plugin: turn that one off.

plugins.name: Phantom Bytecode Viewer
plugins.description: The bytecode of a compiled Java or Kotlin class in the ASM format: select a .java, .kt or .class file, or put the caret in a class, and open View | Show Bytecode. The Bytecode tool window follows the editor's caret and selection to the matching instructions and can hide debug information. Ported from the IntelliJ Community Bytecode Viewer (Apache 2.0) so it updates without a new Phantom build; turn the bundled Bytecode Viewer off if your Phantom still bundles it.

plugins.name: WebP Support
plugins.description: WebP images (lossy, lossless, alpha) open in the image editor and as thumbnails, decoded in Java by the TwelveMonkeys ImageIO reader (BSD) with no native library. Reading only. Replaces the bundled WebP plugin; turn that one off if your Phantom still bundles it. 0.1.1: the WebP decoder loads when a WebP image is first opened, not at startup.

plugins.name: Phantom Modal Commit
plugins.description: The modal commit dialog for Git and Mercurial instead of the Commit tool window: Settings | Advanced Settings | Version Control | Use modal commit interface. Ported from the IntelliJ Community Modal Commit Interface (Apache 2.0) so it updates without a new Phantom build; turn the bundled one off if your Phantom still bundles it.

plugins.name: Phantom CPU Indicator
plugins.description: CPU use of the IDE and the whole machine in the status bar: a one-minute graph and the current numbers, highlighted while the IDE stays busy. Hover it to see what used the IDE's CPU in the last ten seconds (indexing, Kotlin/Java code analysis, GC, JIT, other), the three busiest processes and a thread dump link. Draws without offscreen images and repaints only on change; per-thread analysis and ps run only while hovered or busy. Replaces krasa.cpu.

plugins.name: Phantom Log Console
plugins.description: Readable logs in Run and Debug consoles: a JSON log line (logstash-logback-encoder, ECS, Log4j2 JSON) is shown as time LEVEL [thread] logger : message with its MDC values and the stack trace below; plain text WARN, ERROR and DEBUG lines take their level's console color; a trace id (traceId=, JSON, Spring Boot [traceId-spanId], Sleuth) is a link that lists every console line of that request.

plugins.name: QueryDSL Support
plugins.description: QueryDSL Q classes followed back to their entities: Go to Declaration on a Q class path (order.customer.name, QOrder.order) goes to the entity property or entity, in Java and Kotlin code; Find Usages of a Java entity field also finds its QueryDSL paths; Java entities whose Q class is out of date (a field added or removed since the last build) are reported.

plugins.name: Testcontainers Support
plugins.description: Testcontainers checks for Java and Kotlin tests: a @Container that never starts (no @Testcontainers on its class, or not a container), one started again for every test (an instance field), an image without a version tag or with :latest, and Spring's @DynamicPropertySource methods and @ServiceConnection fields that are not static and so are not found. Java fixes make them static.

plugins.name: Mermaid Support
plugins.description: Editing support and diagram preview for Mermaid in .mmd and .mermaid files and in Markdown code fences: highlighting, completion, formatting, folding, rename and Find Usages of node ids, inspections, and a preview next to the editor. The IntelliJ Community Mermaid plugin (Apache 2.0) under its own id, so Phantom can stop bundling the JetBrains copy (com.intellij.mermaid), which has to be disabled for this one to load. Faster: the preview draws only the latest text after typing pauses and skips text that did not change, Markdown diagrams that did not change are not drawn again (and replaced blocks no longer stay in memory), and mermaid.js is read once and no longer kept stale in the browser after an update.

plugins.name: Phantom TOML
plugins.description: TOML files: highlighting, formatting, folding, references, JSON Schema completion and documentation; Gradle version catalogs build on it. Based on the IntelliJ Community TOML plugin (Apache 2.0); org.toml.lang stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261112 (Nov 12, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom YAML
plugins.description: YAML files: highlighting, formatting, structure view, anchors and aliases, inspections, and JSON Schema completion, validation and documentation; Phantom's docker, kubernetes, openapi and migrations plugins depend on it. Based on the IntelliJ Community YAML plugin (Apache 2.0); org.jetbrains.plugins.yaml stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261112 (Nov 12, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Shell Script
plugins.description: Shell scripts: highlighting, completion, rename, a run configuration, ShellCheck and shfmt, shell blocks in Markdown and the terminal. Based on the IntelliJ Community Shell Script plugin (Apache 2.0); com.jetbrains.sh stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261112 (Nov 12, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Lombok Support
plugins.description: Project Lombok in the editor: generated getters, setters, constructors, builders, loggers and more resolve and complete; lombok.config, inspections, quick fixes and Delombok. Based on the IntelliJ Community Lombok plugin (Apache 2.0); Lombook Plugin stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261112 (Nov 12, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Bytecode Decompiler for Java
plugins.description: Opening a .class file without sources shows Java source decompiled by Fernflower instead of a stub, with the debugger mapping its lines back; Kotlin's bytecode decompiler builds on it. Based on the IntelliJ Community Java Bytecode Decompiler plugin (Apache 2.0); org.jetbrains.java.decompiler stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261112 (Nov 12, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Code Coverage for Java
plugins.description: Run with Coverage for Java run configurations, with the IntelliJ or the JaCoCo runner: the Coverage tool window, line and branch marks in the editor and the Project view, HTML reports and imported reports. Based on the IntelliJ Community Code Coverage for Java plugin (Apache 2.0); Coverage stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261112 (Nov 12, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: TextMate Bundles Support
plugins.description: Highlighting, brace matching, commenting and snippets from TextMate and VS Code grammars for file types no other plugin covers: 22 bundled grammars and any you add. Based on the IntelliJ Community TextMate Bundles plugin (Apache 2.0); org.jetbrains.plugins.textmate stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261112 (Nov 12, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Markdown Support
plugins.description: Markdown files: highlighting, completion, navigation, inspections, table and list editing, images, language injection in code fences, front matter, and the JCEF preview; Shell Script, Kotlin and others build on it. Based on the IntelliJ Community Markdown plugin (Apache 2.0); org.intellij.plugins.markdown stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261112 (Nov 12, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: GitHub Support
plugins.description: GitHub in the IDE: GitHub and GitHub Enterprise accounts (OAuth or token), cloning, Share Project on GitHub, pull requests (list, review with comments in the diff and editor, create, merge), gists, Open on GitHub, and GitHub Actions workflow schemas. Based on the IntelliJ Community GitHub plugin (Apache 2.0); org.jetbrains.plugins.github stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261113 (Nov 13, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: EditorConfig Support
plugins.description: EditorConfig files: properties from .editorconfig applied to the code style, indentation, encoding and trailing spaces of every supported language, plus editing support for the files themselves (highlighting, completion, inspections and quick fixes, navigation, rename, a preview of affected files, and code style scheme export). Based on the IntelliJ Community EditorConfig plugin (Apache 2.0); org.editorconfig.editorconfigjetbrains stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261113 (Nov 13, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Copyright
plugins.description: Copyright notices: profiles with Velocity templates applied to scopes, per-language comment formatting, Update and Generate Copyright actions, updating on save and before commit, and profiles imported from Gradle; Shell Script, Java, Kotlin and others add their file types through it. Based on the IntelliJ Community Copyright plugin (Apache 2.0); com.intellij.copyright stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261113 (Nov 13, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom HTML Tools
plugins.description: HTML editing: inspections for deprecated tags and attributes, accessibility (missing alt, lang, title, form labels), image sizes and unreachable web links, with quick fixes; Update Image Size, table column actions and cell navigation, Go to Symbol for element ids, Extract Include, and image drag and drop. Based on the IntelliJ Community HTML Tools plugin (Apache 2.0); HtmlTools stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261113 (Nov 13, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: TestNG Support
plugins.description: TestNG for Java: run configurations for classes, methods, packages, groups, patterns and suite files with the test tree, forked runs and debugging; test generation; references from dataProvider, dependsOnMethods, groups and testng.xml; inspections and quick fixes such as converting JUnit tests to TestNG. Based on the IntelliJ Community TestNG plugin (Apache 2.0); TestNG-J stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261113 (Nov 13, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Internationalization for Java
plugins.description: Java internationalization: inspections for hard-coded strings, unresolved property keys, message format parameters, inconsistent resource bundles and title capitalization; I18nize to move literals into properties files; folding of message calls to their text; references, find usages and rename between Java and properties keys. Based on the IntelliJ Community Java Internationalization plugin (Apache 2.0); com.intellij.java-i18n stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261113 (Nov 13, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Terminal
plugins.description: The integrated terminal: Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell and cmd sessions in tabs and split panes, shell integration (command blocks, prompt, working directory tracking), command completion from bundled command specs, clickable file links, and commands that open in the IDE; Shell Script and others build on it. Based on the IntelliJ Community Terminal plugin (Apache 2.0); org.jetbrains.plugins.terminal stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261113 (Nov 13, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Grammar
plugins.description: Grammar, style and spelling checks for any text in the IDE: comments, string literals, documentation, commit messages, Markdown, XML, JSON, YAML, properties and plain text, with LanguageTool running locally; English is built in, other languages download when enabled; TOML, YAML, Markdown, Kotlin and others build on it. Built only on open-source code: the IDE layer of the IntelliJ Community Natural Languages plugin (Apache 2.0) and LanguageTool (LGPL 2.1), without JetBrains' closed-source Grazie libraries. Replaces Phantom Natural Languages (dev.phantom.grazie); tanvd.grazi and dev.phantom.grazie stay as aliases, so plugins depending on them keep working. Compared with it: no Grazie rule engine checks or writing style profiles, no auto-fix, no downloaded Hunspell dictionaries for German, Russian and Ukrainian.

plugins.name: Phantom Properties
plugins.description: Properties files: highlighting, formatting, folding, completion, find usages and rename of keys, the Resource Bundle editor, inspections for unused, duplicate, incomplete and unsorted properties, structural search, properties-aware diff and merge, XML properties files and copyright headers; Java I18n, Spring Boot, Grazie, Groovy, Gradle and Maven build on it. Based on the IntelliJ Community Properties plugin (Apache 2.0); com.intellij.properties stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261116 (Nov 16, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: JUnit Support
plugins.description: JUnit 3, 4, 5 and 6 for Java: run configurations for a class, method, package, directory, pattern, tags or unique id, run from the gutter with the test tree, rerun of failed tests, forked runs and debugging; test generation and navigation between a test and its subject; references from @MethodSource, @FieldSource and @EnumSource to their targets; and inspections and quick fixes such as malformed test declarations and JUnit 4 to 5 migration. Based on the IntelliJ Community JUnit plugin (Apache 2.0); JUnit stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261116 (Nov 16, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Repository Search
plugins.description: Dependency completion for Apache Maven pom.xml and Gradle build scripts (group, artifact and version suggestions from the local Maven index, Gradle caches and project modules) and the repository search API Maven and Gradle build on; JetBrains' Package Search service is never called and no usage statistics are collected. Based on the IntelliJ Community Repository Search plugin (Apache 2.0); org.jetbrains.idea.reposearch stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261116 (Nov 16, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom JSON
plugins.description: JSON, JSON5 and JSON Lines files: highlighting, formatting, folding, structure view, Copy JSON Pointer, and JSON Schema mappings, the schemastore.org catalog, completion, validation, documentation and quick fixes; YAML, TOML, OpenAPI and others build on it. Based on the IntelliJ Community JSON plugin (Apache 2.0); com.intellij.modules.json stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261116 (Nov 16, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Gradle DSL Support
plugins.description: A technical plugin with no UI of its own: an API that reads Gradle build files (Groovy, Kotlin script, version catalog TOML) as a model and edits them in place — dependencies, plugins, repositories, ext properties, Android blocks; Gradle-Java's dependency updater and build analysis use it. The Kotlin script parser switches on only with the Kotlin plugin installed. Based on the IntelliJ Community Gradle DSL API plugin (Apache 2.0); org.jetbrains.idea.gradle.dsl stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261116 (Nov 16, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Groovy Scripting Support
plugins.description: The Apache Groovy JSR223 engine for the IDE Scripting Console, and the Groovy 3 library (with Ivy for Grape) that Groovy, Groovy Live Templates and others load through intellij.libraries.groovy. Based on the IntelliJ Community Groovy Scripting plugin (Apache 2.0); com.intellij.groovy.scripting stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261116 (Nov 16, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Groovy Support
plugins.description: Apache Groovy: highlighting, completion, inspections and quick fixes, intentions, refactorings, formatting, structural search, GDSL scripts, Groovy and Gant run configurations with debugger hot swap, the Groovy console, Grape, compilation in the IDE build (Groovy or Eclipse compiler, stub generation), Spock and Geb support, and the Ant, Git and Copyright integrations; Gradle, Maven and others build on it. Based on the IntelliJ Community Groovy plugin (Apache 2.0); org.intellij.groovy stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261116 (Nov 16, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Groovy Live Templates Support
plugins.description: The groovyScript() live template macro: a template variable computed by an Apache Groovy script, inline or from a file, with the macro's arguments and the editor at hand. Based on the IntelliJ Community Groovy Live Templates plugin (Apache 2.0); org.intellij.groovy.live.templates stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261116 (Nov 16, 2026); older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Images
plugins.description: Image files open in a viewer with zoom, grid, transparency chessboard, thumbnails, Set Background Image, external editor and a scientific view (channels, grayscale, binarize, normalize, rotate); SVG files are XML with a preview and Convert SVG to PNG. Based on the IntelliJ Community Images plugin (Apache 2.0), without its usage statistics; com.intellij.platform.images stays as an alias, so plugins depending on it (htmltools, markdown, webp and others) keep working. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261117; older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Local Shared Index
plugins.description: Reuses index data between checkouts of the same project on this machine, so a new worktree or clone does not index files that another checkout already indexed. Nothing leaves the machine. Turn it off by disabling the plugin.

plugins.name: Kotlin Support
plugins.description: Kotlin language support: editing, inspections, refactorings, debugging and Gradle Kotlin DSL scripts. IntelliJ's Kotlin plugin (Apache 2.0) built with each Phantom release; not bundled, since Java-only projects never use it. org.jetbrains.kotlin stays its id, so plugins depending on Kotlin keep working. Built by Phantom from IntelliJ Community sources; not published by JetBrains.

plugins.name: Maven Support
plugins.description: Apache Maven projects: import and sync of pom.xml, the Maven tool window, running goals, pom.xml editing and completion, repositories and indexes. IntelliJ's Maven plugin (Apache 2.0) built with each Phantom release; not bundled, since Gradle projects never use it. org.jetbrains.idea.maven stays its id, so plugins depending on Maven keep working. Built by Phantom from IntelliJ Community sources; not published by JetBrains.

plugins.name: Navigation Bar
plugins.description: The navigation bar: the path of the current file above or below the editor, with popups to browse and open files. Based on the IntelliJ Community Navbar plugin (Apache 2.0); intellij.navbar.plugin stays as an alias and the content module names stay the IntelliJ ones. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261120; older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Recent Files
plugins.description: Recent Files, Recent Locations and the Switcher (Ctrl+Tab). Based on the IntelliJ Community Recent Files plugin (Apache 2.0); intellij.recentFiles.plugin stays as an alias and the content module names stay the IntelliJ ones. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261120; older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Services View
plugins.description: The Services tool window: run configurations, servers, databases, Docker and other services in one place, with the run dashboard. Based on the IntelliJ Community Services View plugin (Apache 2.0); intellij.execution.serviceView.plugin stays as an alias and the content module names stay the IntelliJ ones. Needs Navigation Bar. Bundled with Phantom from build 262.261120; older Phantom builds bundle the IntelliJ plugin instead and don't list it.

plugins.name: Phantom Endpoints
plugins.description: The Endpoints tool window: every HTTP endpoint that installed plugins report (Spring MVC and WebFlux, Ktor, …), grouped by module, with a filter. Enter or double-click opens the handler; Generate HTTP Request adds a request for the endpoint to the scratch file generated-requests.http, with the host and port from the module's Spring Boot or Ktor configuration. Bundled with Phantom (it used to be part of the IDE).
